editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
```

An energy-modeling project quickly accumulates artifacts: models built from
shared repositories, scenarios interpolated from them at different scopes,
and solutions produced by different solvers. energyRt organizes all of it
in one project folder with three principles:

1. **One folder per thing, one manifest per folder.** Every saved model,
   repository, scenario, and solver run is a directory with a small YAML
   manifest describing it. The manifests — not any central database — are
   the source of truth; the project registry is a rebuildable index over
   them.
2. **Share what cannot change.** Models, repositories and datasets are
   stored once, under their **name** (`models/SM/`). An entry under
   development updates in place; **sealing** freezes its content as a
   version identified by a content hash. Only sealed versions are
   referenced -- by models, by scenarios, and by scenarios built on a sealed
   scenario -- so a reference can never point at content that has since
   changed. Everything else is copied into the referring folder.
3. **Derive paths, don't trust stored ones.** Where a run's files live is
   always computed from the scenario's location and the run's identity.
   Loading a scenario re-bases every stored path onto the folder it is
   actually loaded from, so moving or renaming folders — or opening a
   project from a different working directory — just works.

This article walks the whole layout bottom-up. The *Workflow* article shows
the same machinery in day-to-day use; this one explains how the pieces fit.

```{r setup}
library(energyRt)
```

Everything lands under a throwaway project folder here; in a real project
these are relative paths at the project root (the defaults are
`scenarios/`, `models/`, `repositories/`, and `energyRt_registry.csv`).

```{r paths}
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "sm-demo")
set_scenarios_path(file.path(proj, "scenarios"))
set_models_path(file.path(proj, "models"))
set_repositories_path(file.path(proj, "repositories"))
set_registry_file(file.path(proj, "energyRt_registry.csv"))
```

A small model to work with — one region, one technology, three years:

```{r model}
cal <- newCalendar(
  timetable = make_timetable(
    struct = list(ANNUAL = "ANNUAL", HOUR = sprintf("t%02d", 1:4))),
  name = "smc")

make_mod <- function(stock) {
  TECH <- newTechnology(
    "TECH", output = data.frame(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"), cap2act = 1,
    capacity = data.frame(region = "R1", year = 2020:2022, stock = stock),
    fixom = data.frame(fixom = 1),
    vintage = data.frame(olife = 50L), optimizeRetirement = FALSE)
  newModel(
    name = "SM", region = "R1", discount = 0, calendar = cal,
    horizon = newHorizon(2020:2022, intervals = c(1, 1, 1)),
    repo = newRepository(
      "smr", newCommodity("ELC", timeframe = "HOUR"), TECH,
      newSupply("BACK", commodity = "ELC", supply = data.frame(cost = 1000)),
      newDemand("DEM", commodity = "ELC", demand = data.frame(demand = 1))))
}
mod <- make_mod(stock = c(100, 100, 100))
```

# The scenario folder

A **scenario** is one interpolated instance of a model: the model compiled
onto a concrete calendar, horizon, and region scope. Solving it — possibly
several times, with several solvers — produces **runs**. On disk:

```
scenarios/<name-model-calendar-horizon>/
├── scenario.yml        # manifest: model reference, calendar, horizon,
│                       #   `default:` — the default run (edit it freely)
├── scen.RData          # the thin S4 shell (all big data lives beside it)
├── class · format · layout · logfile.csv
├── modInp/parameters/<param>/           # the (base) interpolated problem
├── modOut/variables/<var>/              # the scenario's own solution, once
│                       #   promoted — with modOut.yml recording which run
│                       #   produced it (see "A solution of its own")
├── model/…             # the model's data — only when embedded (see below)
└── runs/               # one folder per solver run
    ├── glpk/                            # a base-problem run
    │   ├── run.yml     #   provenance: solver, cmdline, started/finished,
    │   │               #   duration, status, objective, host, user
    │   ├── input/      #   the exchange tables handed to the solver
    │   ├── output/     #   the solver's raw dump; read_solution() reads it
    │   └── modOut/variables/<var>/      #   the parsed solution store
    └── julia_highs/…                    # another backend, side by side
```

**`output/` and `modOut/` are two tiers, not a copy.** `output/` is the
solver's raw dump, in the backend's own naming and types; `modOut/` is the
imported store, and the import is real work — it normalises the backend away
(GDX, CSV, Arrow and Parquet all land in one place), synthesises the set
aliases no solver writes, types every dimension against its declared members,
and computes `vTechEmsFuel` and `vUserCosts`, which no solver ever produced.
Re-deriving that on demand would also need `@modInp`, which a variant swap may
have replaced — so the store is the answer, not a cache. See `?read_solution`.

Until a solution has been imported, `output/` is the *only* copy of it, which
is why `drop_solver_outputs()` refuses to remove it before then.

Three ideas to notice:

* **A run owns its artifacts.** Solving the same scenario with a second
  backend does not overwrite anything: each run keeps its inputs, raw
  outputs, provenance, and parsed solution. The in-memory scenario object
  holds ONE active solution at a time; switching is a read, not a re-solve.
* **The run's location is derived.** Nothing stores "where run X lives" —
  it is always `<scenario>/runs/<run-id>/`, computed on demand. That is why
  a moved scenario folder cannot strand its runs.
* **`default:` in scenario.yml is yours.** It names the run a bare
  `read_solution(scen)` resolves to after loading; a save sets it to the
  active run, and you may edit the file to point elsewhere.

Let's produce that tree. `run = "<label>"` names a run explicitly; without
it, the label defaults to the solver directory name (e.g. `"glpk"`):

```{r solve}
scen <- interpolate_model(mod, name = "BASE") |>
  solve_scenario(solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE)
scen <- solve_scenario(scen, solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE,
                   force = TRUE, run = "glpk-alt")
scenario_runs(scen)[, c("run", "status", "solver_name", "objective", "active")]
```

`scenario_run_info(scen, "glpk")` returns one run's full `run.yml`;
`read_solution(scen, run = "glpk")` switches the active solution;
`drop_scenario_run(scen, "glpk-alt")` deletes a run (the active one only
with `force = TRUE`). An *external* working directory — outside the
scenario, no run record — is available via
`solve_scenario(solver.dir = "...")`, and `transient = TRUE` solves in a
throwaway folder.

```{r save}
scen <- save_scenario(scen, verbose = FALSE)
sort(list.files(scen@path))
```

The folder *names* — the `<name-model-calendar-horizon>` slug, store entry
basenames, the default solve label — are derived by built-in functions you
can override with `set_path_builder()` (see the toolbox below). Custom
names are safe because nothing is ever parsed back out of a folder name:
scenarios and store entries are found by the name recorded in their
manifests and the registry. The run *tree* (`runs/<variant>/<solve>/`) is
structural and not overridable.

# Models, repositories and datasets: versions and references

The model is part of the scenario, but fifty scenarios built on one model do
not need fifty copies of it. A model is saved once in the **model store**,
under its name:

```{r model-store}
save_model(mod, verbose = FALSE)
list_versions("SM", type = "model")
```

While a model is being developed, its entry updates in place: saving a
changed model rewrites `models/SM/`, and the manifest records a save id
rather than a content hash, so a large model is not serialised for hashing
on every save. Saving identical content is a no-op.

**Sealing** turns the current content into a version. `seal_model()`
computes the content hash (`model_hash()`, with all volatile bookkeeping
stripped) and moves the payload into a version folder,
`models/SM/<hash>/`, which no later save changes. Changed content under a
sealed name requires `unseal_model()` first; the sealed version stays, and
whatever references it keeps loading it.

```{r model-seal}
seal_model(mod, verbose = FALSE)
list_versions("SM", type = "model")
```

**Only sealed versions are referenced.** A scenario records the model it was
interpolated from. When that model is a sealed version, `save_scenario()`
stores the reference `{name, hash}` instead of a copy, and the sealed version
lists the scenario among its dependents:

```{r model-ref}
scen <- save_scenario(scen, verbose = FALSE)
yaml::read_yaml(file.path(scen@path, "scenario.yml"))$model[c("name", "source")]
list_dependents("SM", type = "model")[, c("type", "name", "version")]
```

A model that is not sealed is copied into the scenario folder (`model/`), so
a later change to the store cannot alter a saved scenario;
`save_scenario(mode = "full")` (or `options(energyRt.save_mode = "full")`)
copies everything in regardless, for a folder that must be self-contained.

A scenario keeps the model **as given** in `@model`, with the repositories
added at interpolation (`interpolate_model(mod, <objects>)`) as the
scenario's own. The expanded copy that interpolation works on -- vintage and
cluster variants, resource tiers, materialised weather transforms, a
spatial cut -- is rebuilt when a reader needs it. The reference to a sealed
model therefore holds for models with variants and for sampled scenarios
alike, and the scenario's own repositories travel with it.

The same rules apply one level down to **repositories**
(`save_repository()`, `seal_repository()`): a model referencing a sealed
repository version, or a selection of its objects, records `{name, hash}`.
The **dataset store** (`datasets/`) holds tables saved explicitly with
`save_dataset()` -- a weather series, a geoscale map -- and the tables of
models and repositories that match one of them by content. A dataset keeps
every version by content, a dataset can also record its *generating call*
(`save_dataset(name = , fun = "pkg::fun", args = )`), and a version that
another entry references is never rewritten in place.

The versioning logic in a few lines:

```{r hash-logic, eval = FALSE}
model_hash(mod)                       # content identity (misc and paths stripped);
                                      #   repository_hash(), dataset_hash(),
                                      #   object_hash() for anything else
save_model(mod)                       # unchanged -> no-op; changed -> updated in place
seal_model(mod)                       # the current content becomes a version
load_model("SM", hash = "a1b2c3d4")   # a sealed version by (short) hash
list_versions()                       # models, repositories, datasets:
                                      #   status, sealed_at, refs, size
list_dependents("SM", type = "model") # what references its versions
```

# Scenarios built on a base

A policy scenario usually differs from a reference scenario by a few
objects: a cap, a tax, a technology, or a coarser sample of the same
problem. `interpolate_model(..., base = REF)` builds it on the interpolated
REF instead of from scratch:

```{r base}
fee <- newCosts("FEE", variable = "vTechAct", mult = 2,
                subset = list(tech = "TECH"))
scen_fee <- interpolate_model(mod, fee, name = "FEE", base = scen)
```

What is reused depends on what is added:

| added to REF | how the scenario is built |
|---|---|
| constraints, cost terms, taxes, subsidies | REF's tables are copied; only the rows of the additions are computed |
| new technologies, storages, supplies, trades, commodities | REF's per-object tables are reused, the new objects' tables computed, every map rebuilt |
| a calendar of some of REF's timeslices, or a filtered geoscale | REF's tables are taken filtered to the sample; boundary stubs are computed |
| anything else (another model, a replaced object, another horizon or setting) | interpolated in full, with a message naming the reason |

In every case the result equals a full interpolation of the model with REF's
additions and the new ones, which `compare_inputs()` confirms:

```{r base-check}
full <- interpolate_model(mod, fee, name = "FEE_FULL")
sum(compare_inputs(scen_fee, full)$summary$status != "identical")
```

The scenario's manifest names its base (`base:`). When REF is saved and
**sealed**, `save_scenario()` stores a reference to each of REF's tables that
the new scenario shares -- with a row filter for a sample of REF -- and keeps
only the tables that differ. `list_dependents(REF)` then lists the scenarios
built on it, and `unseal_scenario(REF)` refuses while they exist:

```{r base-seal, eval = FALSE}
seal_scenario(scen)                    # REF, saved, becomes a base
scen_fee <- save_scenario(scen_fee)    # shared tables referenced, the rest kept
list_dependents(scen)                  # FEE
unseal_scenario(scen)                  # refused while FEE references it
```

A base that is not sealed is never referenced: its tables are copied, and a
message says so.

# The registry

Every save also records its object in the project **registry** — one CSV at
the project root indexing models, repositories, scenarios, and runs:

```{r registry}
reg <- load_registry()
reg[, c("type", "name", "parent")]
```

The registry is an *index, never an authority*: `refresh_registry()`
rebuilds it at any time by rescanning the stores and reading the manifests.
`find_in_registry(reg, type = "model", hash = "a1b2")` looks entries up by
type, name, (short) hash — or, for run rows, by `variant =`: a run's `name`
holds the plain solve label, its problem sits in the `variant` column, and
`parent` names the scenario (the worked example below shows a full table).

The registry is also what makes NAME-based access work. `getScenario("BASE")`
resolves the name, loads the thin on-disk shell, and caches it in the
session bank `.scen` — re-saved scenarios reload automatically, repeat
access is free. `getData()` accepts names directly, so comparing registered
scenarios needs no explicit loading at all:

```{r getdata-by-name}
getData("BASE", name = "vObjective", merge = TRUE)[, c("scenario", "value")]
```

`getModel()`, `getRepository()` and `getDataset()` are the typed
companions; `load_scenarios()` returns many scenarios as a `getData()`-ready
named list; and `open_project("path/")` points a session at another
project's registry and stores in one call.

# Variants: several problems in one scenario

A scenario sometimes needs *the same model asked a different question* —
a sampled calendar, a restricted horizon, a recursive step with carried-over
capacity. These are **own-problem variants**: named folders under `runs/`
that carry their *own* interpolated problem, with their solves inside.

```{r variant}
scen_low <- interpolate_model(make_mod(c(50, 50, 50)), name = "BASE",
                              overwrite = TRUE) |>
  solve_scenario(solver = solver_options$glpk, echo = FALSE, variant = "low")
scen_low <- save_scenario(scen_low, verbose = FALSE)
scenario_runs(scen_low)[, c("run", "variant", "modinp", "objective")]
```

```
runs/
├── glpk/  glpk-alt/     # base-problem runs (modinp: shared)
└── low/                 # an own-problem variant
    ├── variant.yml      #   what this problem IS (type, horizon, calendar;
    │                    #   drivers add fields like sequence/step)
    ├── modInp/          #   ITS parameter store — written once, shared by
    ├── variant.RData    #   all of the variant's solves
    └── glpk/…           #   its runs, same shape as any run
```

The base problem's store stays untouched at the scenario level.
`read_solution(scen, run = "glpk")` vs `run = "low/glpk"` switches not just
the solution but the whole in-memory *problem* — settings and parameters
swap together, in both directions — so `getData()` is always consistent
with the run you are looking at. This is the storage substrate for the
recursive solver: `solve_recursive()` keeps a whole year-by-year
sequence as one scenario with one variant per step.

### A solution of its own

A solved scenario's results live in the run that produced them, and the object
points there. That makes `runs/` load-bearing: delete it and every read fails,
because the store the scenario names is gone.

`promote_solution()` copies the chosen run's solution to `<scenario>/modOut/`,
beside `modInp/`, and clears the active run so the scenario reads from there:

```{r promote, eval = FALSE}
scenario_solutions(scen)                  # which attempt to keep?
scen <- promote_solution(scen, "glpk")    # or import_solution(..., promote = TRUE)
drop_scenario_run(scen, "glpk", force = TRUE)   # the run is now scratch
```

After that the run tree is disposable. `modOut.yml` travels with the store and
records which run produced the solution, its objective, stage, solver and
timings — provenance that otherwise lives only in `run.yml` and would go with
the run folder. Its presence is also how a complete store is told from a
half-written one, and how `upgrade_scenario_layout()` knows not to migrate a
promoted store back under a run.

Promoting copies rather than moves, so comparing attempts keeps working until
you drop them. A **variant** cannot be promoted: its `modInp` and settings
live inside `runs/<variant>/`, so lifting only its solution would pair variant
results with the base problem's parameters.

### Getting data out of a variant

`getData(run = )` reads a run directly, tagging the rows with a `run` column:

```{r variant-data, eval = FALSE}
getData(scen, "vTechOut", merge = TRUE, run = "low/glpk")
getData(scen, "vTechOut", merge = TRUE, run = c("glpk", "low/glpk"))
getData(scen, "vTechOut", merge = TRUE, run = "all")
```

Each run is read on a *copy*, so the object keeps its active run, and a
variant brings its whole problem with it — parameters included. Spanning runs
of different problems warns: a variant has its own `modInp`, so those numbers
are not like-for-like. Without `run`, `getData()` reads the active run and
adds no column, exactly as before; `read_solution(scen, run = )` still
switches the object itself when that is what you want.

`compare_scenarios(scen, runs = c("glpk", "low/glpk"))` does the switching for
you and tabulates the runs side by side — note that it compares *runs*, which
may be variants, even though an assumption change belongs in its own scenario
(below).

A variant's solution lives with its run, at
`runs/<variant>/<solve>/modOut/`, exactly like a base run's. Saving while a
variant is active writes that variant's problem and leaves the others alone;
loading re-activates whatever `default:` names.

Each driver records how it produced a variant in `runs/<variant>/variant.yml`
— `type:` naming the method and `params:` its settings. Re-running a driver
over an existing sequence with *different* settings is refused rather than
silently replacing it; `overwrite = TRUE` proceeds.

To remove one, `drop_scenario_run(scen, "<variant>")` deletes the **whole
variant folder** — its `modInp/`, its manifest and every solve inside it.
Sealing is scenario-wide, not per variant.

### Two unrelated things called "variant"

This section is about **run variants**: own-problem folders under `runs/`.
Unrelated to them, a technology can have vintage and cluster **variants** —
`getVariants()`, `variantSummary()`, `getData(variants = TRUE)`,
`levcost(by_variant = )`. Those describe processes inside one problem and have
nothing to do with the run tree. The word is overloaded; the two never meet.

## Scenario, variant, or run?

The three axes have crisp definitions — *what changed decides where it
lives*:

| what changed | it is a… | lives at |
|---|---|---|
| solver, tolerances, method, threads | **run** | `runs/[<variant>/]<label>/` |
| the *scope* of the same declarations — a sampled calendar, a region subset or aggregation, a horizon window, a recursive step | **variant** (own problem) | `runs/<variant>/` with its own `modInp` |
| *assumptions or declarations* — a fuel price, a policy cap, a technology's cost | **scenario** (built on a reference with `base =`) | its own folder |

Two runs of one problem agree on every number going in; anything that
changes the calendar or geoscale changes the compiled LP and is therefore
a different *problem*, never a different run -- a variant inside the
scenario, or a scenario of its own built on the full one with `base =`;
and an assumption change deserves its own scenario — that is the level `compare_scenarios()`
compares, with its own registry identity. Run and variant names are
**labels** (dashes allowed: `glpk-alt`); scenario/model/dataset names are
**object names** and follow the name rule (letters, digits, underscore).

# A worked example: a TOPIA project

A project with two policy scenarios (`BASE`, `CO2CAP`) on the all-regions
model `TOPIA_R11`, solved at full and sampled time resolution, for region
subsets, and for a one-region continental aggregation:

```
topia-project/
├── energyRt_registry.csv                 the index (rebuildable)
├── datasets/
│   ├── topia_weather/  topia_demand/   big tables — stored ONCE
│   └── topia_map/                       the Geoscale (rds)
├── repositories/
│   └── topia_r11/                       kit repo; tables as dataset refs
├── models/
│   └── TOPIA_R11/                       ONE folder per name
│       └── <hash>/                      the sealed version scenarios reference
├── scenarios/
│   ├── BASE-TOPIA_R11-d365_h24/         {scenario}-{model}-{calendar}
│   │   ├── scenario.yml · scen.RData     manifest · identity + BASE problem
│   │   ├── modInp/                       base problem's parameters
│   │   └── runs/
│   │       ├── julia_highs/              base-problem solve, full year
│   │       ├── s4_h24/                   VARIANT: sampled calendar
│   │       │   ├── variant.yml · variant.RData · modInp/
│   │       │   ├── glpk/  glpk-barrier/  its solves
│   │       ├── r3/   r1/                 VARIANTS: region subsets
│   │       │   └── … · glpk/
│   │       └── c1/                       VARIANT: continental aggregation
│   │           └── … · julia_highs/
│   ├── CO2CAP-TOPIA_R11-d365_h24/       the policy scenario, built on the
│   │   │                                 sealed BASE (base = BASE): it
│   │   │                                 references BASE's tables and keeps
│   │   │                                 only those the cap changes
│   │   └── runs/julia_highs/  s4_h24/…   cuts actually solved
│   └── CHEAPGAS-TOPIA_R11-d365_h24/     an ASSUMPTION change = scenario
└── reports/  levcosts/                   derived-artifact tiers
```

Reading the tree with the definitions above: `s4_h24`, `r3`, `r1` and `c1`
are variants *because* their calendar or geoscale differs; `glpk` and
`glpk-barrier` are runs *because* only the solver differs; `CHEAPGAS` is a
scenario *because* an input price changed. The continental aggregation is
a problem *of `TOPIA_R11`* — aggregation happens at interpolation, and
`variant.yml` records the coarse geoscale as provenance (only an
explicitly built and stored aggregate model would earn its own `models/`
entry). The weather year exists exactly once, in `datasets/`, referenced
up the chain.

The registry indexes it all — one plain row per thing, run rows carrying
the solve label in `name` and the problem in `variant`:

| type | name | parent | variant | path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dataset | `topia_weather` | | | `datasets/topia_weather` |
| repository | `topia_r11` | | | `repositories/topia_r11` |
| model | `TOPIA_R11` | | | `models/TOPIA_R11` |
| scenario | `BASE` | | | `scenarios/BASE-TOPIA_R11-d365_h24` |
| run | `julia_highs` | `BASE` | | `…/runs/julia_highs` |
| run | `glpk` | `BASE` | `s4_h24` | `…/runs/s4_h24/glpk` |
| run | `glpk-barrier` | `BASE` | `s4_h24` | `…/runs/s4_h24/glpk-barrier` |
| run | `glpk` | `BASE` | `r3` | `…/runs/r3/glpk` |
| run | `julia_highs` | `BASE` | `c1` | `…/runs/c1/julia_highs` |
| scenario | `CO2CAP` | | | `scenarios/CO2CAP-TOPIA_R11-d365_h24` |
| run | `julia_highs` | `CO2CAP` | | `…/runs/julia_highs` |

Typical queries against it:

```{r topia-queries, eval = FALSE}
reg <- load_registry()
find_in_registry(reg, type = "run", parent = "BASE", variant = "s4_h24")
find_in_registry(reg, type = "run", variant = "")     # all base-problem runs
getData(c("BASE", "CO2CAP", "CHEAPGAS"),           # compare by NAME alone
        name = "vEmsFuelTot", comm = "CO2", merge = TRUE)
read_solution(getScenario("BASE"), run = "s4_h24/glpk")  # activate a variant run
```

# Moving folders, older layouts

Because run and store locations are derived and manifests travel with their
folders, the whole project directory can be moved, renamed, or synced
between machines. `load_scenario()` re-bases all paths onto wherever the
folder actually is — and if data genuinely is not where the object expects
it, the failure is an *error naming the fix*, never silently empty results.

Folders written by older energyRt versions (the pre-`runs/` layout with
`script/<solver>/` directories) still load, and migrate in place with one
idempotent call:

```r
upgrade_scenario_layout("scenarios/OLD")
```

which moves each solver directory into `runs/`, backfills the provenance
records from what is on disk, and writes the current manifests.

# Lifecycle: sealing and the deletion queue

Because entries update in place, finished work is locked by sealing:
`seal_model("SM")` (and `seal_repository()`, `seal_dataset()`,
`seal_scenario()`) freezes the entry -- identical re-saves stay silent
no-ops, changed content errors until the matching `unseal_*()`. A sealed
scenario is an archive: it loads, `getData()`s and reports freely, but
refuses re-saves, new recorded solves, and `drop_scenario_run()`. Sealing
the inputs of published work keeps a model from drifting out from under the
scenarios that reference it.

Unsealing checks what depends on the entry: `unseal_model()` and
`unseal_repository()` list the dependents of the current sealed version and
refuse unless `force = TRUE` (the version itself stays, so the dependents
keep loading it); `unseal_scenario()` refuses while scenarios built on it
reference its tables. `list_dependents(x)` shows the same list at any time,
`recursive = TRUE` following it from a repository through models to
scenarios.

The other end of the lifecycle is a soft-delete queue:
`mark_delete(x, importance = )` tags an entry (higher importance = more
valuable = deleted later), `unmark_delete()` clears the tag, and
`delete_marked()` -- **dry-run by default** -- removes marked entries up to
an importance threshold. Sealed entries are never deleted, even when
marked, and neither is anything another entry references.

Superseded versions are listed by `list_versions()` with a status --
`current`, `in use` (referenced), `marked`, `unused` -- and are removed only
when marked: `mark_delete(x, version = "unused")` marks every version
nothing references, `mark_delete(x, version = "<hash>")` one of them, and
`delete_marked()` deletes those still unreferenced. A dataset version that
another entry references is likewise never rewritten in place by
`save_dataset(rehash = FALSE)` or `overwrite = TRUE`.

# The toolbox

The storage API by task — every verb resolves registered NAMES, never
paths:

```{r toolbox, eval = FALSE}
## anchor a session on a project (registry + all store roots + tiers)
open_project("path/to/project")
get_scenarios_path(); get_models_path(); get_repositories_path()
get_datasets_path(); get_reports_path(); get_levcost_cache_path()

## save — identical content is a no-op; changed content updates in place
save_model(mod);  save_repository(repo);  save_dataset(x, "wsol")
save_scenario(scen)                    # embed_model / embed_repos /
                                       #   embed_datasets = NULL|TRUE|FALSE
save_dataset(name = "kit", fun = "energyRt::topia_profiles",
             args = list(regions = "R1"))   # store the CALL + a snapshot

## load (explicit IO) and get* (name-first, scenario shells cached in .scen)
load_model("TOPIA_R11");  load_scenario("BASE");  load_scenarios()
getScenario("BASE");  getModel("TOPIA_R11");  getDataset("wsol")
getData(c("BASE", "CO2CAP"), name = "vTechOut", merge = TRUE)

## runs and problems
scenario_runs(scen)                    # incl. variant, peak_mb, updated
scenario_run_info(scen, "glpk")        # one run's full run.yml
read_solution(scen, run = "s4_h24/glpk")   # activate problem + solution
drop_scenario_run(scen, "glpk-alt")
solve_scenario(scen, variant = "low")  # solve as an own-problem variant

## the registry
reg <- load_registry()
find_in_registry(reg, type = "run", parent = "BASE", variant = "s4_h24")
refresh_registry()                     # rebuild the index from manifests

## scenarios built on a base
interpolate_model(mod, cap, name = "CO2CAP", base = scen_base)
interpolate_model(mod, cal_sample, name = "BASE_S", base = scen_base)

## lifecycle
seal_model("TOPIA_R11");  seal_scenario("BASE")     # freeze as versions
unseal_scenario("BASE")                # refused while scenarios build on it
list_versions()                        # versions with status, refs, size
list_dependents("TOPIA_R11", type = "model", recursive = TRUE)
mark_delete("OLD", type = "scenario", importance = 1)
mark_delete("TOPIA_R11", type = "model", version = "unused")
delete_marked()                        # DRY RUN by default
delete_marked(max_importance = 1, dry_run = FALSE)

## bookkeeping
set_log_file("energyRt_log.csv");  read_log()       # operation log
upgrade_scenario_layout("scenarios/OLD")            # migrate old folders

## custom folder names (session-local hooks; see ?path_builders)
set_path_builder(
  scenario_dir = \(name, model, calendar, horizon)  # scenario folder slug
    paste(name, calendar, sep = "."),
  store_entry  = \(type, name) paste0(type, "_", name),  # store basenames
  run_label    = \(solver)                          # default solve label
    if (is.null(solver$name)) "run" else solver$name
)
set_path_builder(scenario_dir = FALSE)              # FALSE removes one hook
```

# Summary of the vocabulary

| thing | where | identity | manifest |
|---|---|---|---|
| repository | `repositories/<name>/`, sealed versions in `<name>/<hash>/` | name (hash verifies) | `repository.yml` |
| model | `models/<name>/`, sealed versions in `<name>/<hash>/` | name (hash verifies) | `model.yml` |
| dataset | `datasets/<name>/<hash>/`, one folder per version | name (hash verifies) | `dataset.yml` |
| scenario | `scenarios/<slug>/` | name | `scenario.yml` |
| variant (own problem) | `<scenario>/runs/<variant>/` | name within scenario | `variant.yml` |
| run (solve) | `<scenario>/runs/[<variant>/]<solve>/` | run id `"<solve>"` / `"<variant>/<solve>"` | `run.yml` |
| registry | `energyRt_registry.csv` | — (rebuildable index) | — |

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(proj, recursive = TRUE)
```
